investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T20:27:54Z with an identical 409 conflict response from POST /api/agents: "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe's createAgent call is being rejected by the production Swarm API before any agent is provisioned, so zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and all contract assertions are unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.
investigation.rootCause: The Swarm backend is enforcing a hard per-org (or per-account) agent quota of 100 and is rejecting new agent creation requests with HTTP 409. The observability probe account has reached or exceeded this limit, so every call to POST /api/agents made by the eval runner returns "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" before an agent is created. Because agent creation is the first step in all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime), all three fail with the same message and produce no evidence. The quota exhaustion is the shared upstream dependency failure identified by the sibling correlation signal.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1539 — the call returned in ~1.5 s, consistent with a fast quota-rejection response rather than a timeout or VM provisioning delay.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Probe/eval account has accumulated 100 or more remote agents in the Swarm backend (from prior eval runs, leaked cleanup, or stale agents) and the quota ceiling is now blocking all new creation attempts. This is directly stated in the 409 body and is consistent with all three sibling checks failing identically.

SECONDARY — The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (source-context run-status-probes.mjs:1256) may have failed to delete agents from previous runs (e.g., due to prior eval crashes or network errors), causing agents to accumulate until the quota was hit.
TERTIARY — The Swarm backend quota limit of 100 may have been lowered by a backend configuration change, causing the probe account to exceed the new limit even if cleanup was functioning correctly.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Commit d58f85f (feat(observability): expand feature health eval coverage, 2026-06-15T20:04:18Z) touched eval runner and workflow files ~23 minutes before the failure. However, d58f85f's touched paths are CI/workflow files with no matched needles against the failing check, and the failure message is a backend quota error rather than a runner logic error. This commit is a low-confidence hypothesis only and is not supported by the eval error message or source excerpts.
